cities.base: The Parkway and Elephant's Walk end of town, not the lodges out on the Bulawayo road. From there the Rain Forest gate is a fifteen minute walk, the bridge and the Zambian border are twenty five, and y
cities.name: Victoria Falls town

cities.base: The riverside strip on the Mosi-oa-Tunya Road between town and the falls entrance, around Sichango and the Zambezi Sun. You are ten minutes from the Knife Edge and ten from the restaurants on the main
cities.name: Livingstone

cities.base: Split it. Two nights at a river camp near Mfuwe Gate for the leopard drives and the night drives, then two nights in a bushcamp in the Nsefu sector or on the Luwi, where walking is the whole activity
cities.name: South Luangwa

cities.base: The riverfront between the Chongwe confluence and Jeki, which is where the canoeing and the boat work happen. Chiawa, Sausage Tree, Old Mondoro and Anabezi are all on the bank inside the park; Royal Z
cities.name: the Lower Zambezi

cities.base: The Zambezi terrace between Mucheni and Nyamepi, under the albida. That strip is where the walking is, where the canoes put in, and where the elephant come up onto their hind legs. Kanga Pan is 30 km
cities.name: Mana Pools

cities.base: The southern concessions around the Kennedy line and Makalolo, which is where the pumped pans and the elephant are. Somalisa, Davison's, Little Makalolo, Linkwasha and The Hide are all in that block,
cities.name: Hwange

places.name: Devil's Cataract and the Livingstone statue
places.note: The western end of the gorge and the one viewpoint that still has water over it in November, which is why it is the first stop on the Zimbabwe path in every month of the year.
places.neighborhood: Victoria Falls National Park, west end of the Rain Forest

places.name: Main Falls viewpoint
places.note: The widest curtain and the one worth timing: in April the spray here is heavy enough that you see white and hear thunder and nothing else, in October you see the whole 100 metre drop and the rock behind it.
places.neighborhood: Victoria Falls National Park, Rain Forest path stops 4 to 7

places.name: Danger Point
places.note: An unfenced rock shelf out over the second gorge with the bridge to your left, slippery and genuinely dangerous in high water and the best angle on the whole system in low.
places.neighborhood: Victoria Falls National Park, east end of the Rain Forest pa

places.name: the Rain Forest walk, statue to Danger Point
places.note: Sixteen numbered viewpoints along two kilometres of wet path; from February to June bring a rain jacket and a dry bag because the spray is rain, and from September to December bring nothing because the forest is dry and half the cataracts are bare rock.
places.neighborhood: Victoria Falls National Park, Livingstone Way entrance

places.name: Victoria Falls Bridge and the bridge tour
places.note: A 1905 steel arch across the gorge that you can walk for free between the two immigration posts, or pay to go under the deck on the catwalk with a guide who knows the construction story.
places.neighborhood: the Zimbabwe and Zambia border, below the second gorge

places.name: The Lookout Cafe
places.note: Built on the gorge edge above the rafting put-in, so you eat a decent burger while watching people gorge-swing past the table, and the view is better than the kitchen.
places.neighborhood: Batoka Gorge rim, off the Zambezi Drive above the boiling po

places.name: Stanley's Terrace at the Victoria Falls Hotel
places.note: High tea on a colonial lawn with the bridge framed at the end of it, which is either exactly what you came for or exactly what you did not, and either way it costs about USD 30 for two.
places.neighborhood: Mallet Drive, the old hotel lawn facing the bridge

places.name: The Boma at Victoria Falls Safari Lodge
places.note: A buffet with drumming, face paint and a mopane worm dare, run at scale for coaches, and the game meat is genuinely well cooked if you can take the theatre.
places.neighborhood: Victoria Falls Safari Lodge, Squire Cummings Road

places.name: The Three Monkeys
places.note: Where the guides and raft crews eat on their nights off, with a short menu of pizza, curry and steak and a bar that stays open later than the rest of town.
places.neighborhood: Elephant's Walk end of town, near Victoria Falls station

places.name: The SmokeHouse and River Brewing Co
places.note: The only place in either town brewing its own beer, in an old town building with a smoker out the back, and the brisket is worth the wait if they have not sold out.
places.neighborhood: central Victoria Falls, off Livingstone Way

places.name: the Zambezi National Park river drive
places.note: Six kilometres upstream of the town gate and almost nobody drives it, which buys you sable, elephant and a quiet stretch of river for the USD 18 park fee plus the vehicle.
places.neighborhood: Zambezi National Park, the riverside loop upstream of the fa

places.name: the walk-with-lions encounter
places.note: Captive-raised lions on a lead rope walked past paying tourists, sold as conservation and questioned by every serious conservation body in the region, so put the money into the Zambezi National Park drive instead.
places.neighborhood: Masuwe, on the Bulawayo road out of town

places.name: Knife Edge Bridge
places.note: A narrow footbridge straight into the spray facing the Eastern Cataract: from February to July you will be soaked through in ninety seconds and see very little, and from September to December you will be dry and looking at a wall of bare basalt.
places.neighborhood: Mosi-oa-Tunya National Park, Zambian falls side

places.name: the Boiling Pot descent
places.note: Twenty minutes of steep switchbacks down to the whirlpool where the river turns under the bridge, hot on the way back up, and the one place you stand at the bottom of the gorge without paying for a raft.
places.neighborhood: Mosi-oa-Tunya National Park, the zigzag path below the Knife

places.name: the Eastern Cataract viewpoint
places.note: The Zambian third of the falls and the honest test of your timing, because this is the section that runs dry first and by late October and November it is rock with a trickle at the end.
places.neighborhood: Mosi-oa-Tunya National Park, above the Zambian lip

places.name: Livingstone Island and Devil's Pool
places.note: The only licensed way onto the island on the lip, and the pool itself only opens when the river drops, roughly mid-August to mid-January depending on the year; outside that window you are booking a breakfast on an island with no swim.
places.neighborhood: mid-river on the lip of the falls, boat from the Dry Manzi j

places.name: the Victoria Falls Field Museum
places.note: One room built over an excavation showing how the river has cut back through eight gorges in the basalt, and it explains the landscape you just walked past better than any guide will.
places.neighborhood: inside the Zambian falls entrance, beside the curio stalls

places.name: the Livingstone Museum
places.note: Zambia's oldest museum, with Livingstone's own letters and a colonial history section that is franker than most in the region, in a building that badly needs money.
places.neighborhood: Mosi-oa-Tunya Road, central Livingstone

places.name: the Mosi-oa-Tunya park rhino drive
places.note: A small fenced riverside block with an armed-escort white rhino group, which is the only rhino on this whole route and takes about two hours including the tracking walk.
places.neighborhood: Mosi-oa-Tunya National Park, upstream game section off the N

places.name: Cafe Zambezi
places.note: A courtyard doing Zambian plates alongside pizza, with crocodile and village chicken on the same menu and a bar that fills with river guides after dark.
places.neighborhood: Mosi-oa-Tunya Road, central Livingstone

places.name: Olga's Italian Corner
places.note: Wood-fired pizza run as a training kitchen for a local youth project, cheap and consistently the best value meal in either town.
places.neighborhood: corner of Mosi-oa-Tunya Road and Nakatindi Road

places.name: sundowners on the Royal Livingstone lawn
places.note: A deck on the river about 400 metres above the drop, where you watch the spray column go pink and zebra walk between the tables, and non-guests can drink there without a fight.
places.neighborhood: the Royal Livingstone Hotel deck, upstream of the lip

places.name: Maramba Market
places.note: The town's real food market, chitenge cloth and dried kapenta and no curio stalls at all, and you will be the only visitor in it.
places.neighborhood: Maramba township, north-east of the town centre

places.name: Mukuni Village
places.note: The Leya chieftaincy that predates the town, now run as a scripted tour that ends in a craft yard with a hard sell, and the cultural content does not survive it.
places.neighborhood: Mukuni, 10 km east of the falls

places.name: Mfuwe Gate and the Luangwa bridge
places.note: The bridge over the Luangwa at the gate holds hippo in the pool below it all dry season and is where every drive starts, so you will cross it four times a day and never mind.
places.neighborhood: Mfuwe Gate, the park's main eastern entrance

places.name: Mfuwe Lagoon
places.note: A permanent oxbow that shrinks through the dry season until the hippo are stacked in it, and in late October and November the elephant walk through the lodge reception to reach the mangoes behind it.
places.neighborhood: in front of Mfuwe Lodge, inside the gate

places.name: Luangwa Wafwa
places.note: A dead meander that fills in the rains and holds water long after the plains dry, which by September makes it the best single place in the park to sit and wait rather than drive.
places.neighborhood: Nsefu sector, an old oxbow cut off from the main river

places.name: the Nsefu salt pan and the crowned crane colony
places.note: Warm saline springs seeping into an open pan where several hundred crowned cranes stand at first light, and the ground is soft enough that you approach on foot rather than in the vehicle.
places.neighborhood: Nsefu sector, the hot springs and salt pan north of Nsefu Ca

places.name: Lion Plain
places.note: Open ground with enough sightlines to actually watch a hunt develop rather than arrive after it, and the resident prides here are the reason people book the Nsefu sector over Mfuwe.
places.neighborhood: Nsefu sector, the open grassland between the river and the t

places.name: the Kaingo hippo hide
places.note: A two-tier hide dug into the bank a few metres from a pod of about sixty, so you are at eye level with them yawning and fighting, and it is Shenton guests only.
places.neighborhood: Kaingo Camp, the Luangwa riverbank north of Nsefu

places.name: the carmine bee-eater banks
places.note: Thousands of southern carmine bee-eaters nest in vertical holes in the riverbank and the colony only exists from about early September to early November, so it is a date, not a place.
places.neighborhood: the eroding Luangwa riverbanks near Kaingo and Mwamba

places.name: Mwamba's Last Waterhole hide
places.note: A sunken hide on the last water left in a dry sand river, where you sit through the middle of the day and let elephant, buffalo and whatever follows them come to you.
places.neighborhood: Mwamba Bushcamp, on the Mwamba River sand

places.name: the bar under the mango trees at Mfuwe Lodge
places.note: A thatched bar over the lagoon where the hippo start calling around six, and in the mango weeks the elephant genuinely do walk between the chairs.
places.neighborhood: Mfuwe Lodge, above the lagoon

places.name: Tribal Textiles
places.note: A hand-painted cloth workshop employing around a hundred people from the villages along the road, and you can walk the dyeing sheds before you buy anything.
places.neighborhood: the Mfuwe road, about 8 km from the gate

places.name: the Jackalberry restaurant at Flatdogs
places.note: The one place near the gate that will feed non-residents properly, under an ebony grove with elephant walking through the campsite most evenings in October.
places.neighborhood: Flatdogs Camp, the riverbank just outside Mfuwe Gate

places.name: Chipembele Wildlife Education Trust
places.note: A conservation education centre that teaches thousands of Zambian schoolchildren a year, and the visit is a straight talk on snaring and human wildlife conflict rather than an animal show.
places.neighborhood: the Luangwa bank downstream of Mfuwe village

places.name: the Chongwe River confluence
places.note: A sand bar at the meeting of two rivers under the escarpment, where elephant cross in the late afternoon and the light comes off the water from the west.
places.neighborhood: the western park boundary where the Chongwe meets the Zambez

places.name: the Jeki floodplain
places.note: Open grass between the river and the escarpment with the highest game density in the park, and the airstrip sits in the middle of it so your first sighting is often on the drive from the plane.
places.neighborhood: around Jeki airstrip, the central park floodplain

places.name: the Chifungulu Channel
places.note: A narrow backwater you paddle rather than motor, shallow enough that hippo have nowhere to go around you, which is exactly why the guide keeps you tight to the bank.
places.neighborhood: a side channel of the Zambezi behind the islands

places.name: the Anabezi winterthorn forest
places.note: Tall winterthorn with almost no understorey, so you see elephant at 300 metres through open woodland, and the east of the park gets a fraction of the vehicles the Jeki end does.
places.neighborhood: the eastern end of the park near the Mushika River

places.name: the Zambezi escarpment overlook
places.note: A climb onto the rift wall behind the camps for the one view that shows you the whole valley and Mana Pools on the far bank, and it is hot and steep enough that most people never do it.
places.neighborhood: the inland ridge above the floodplain

places.name: the river deck at Chiawa Camp
places.note: The oldest camp in the park and its deck sits low on the water, so sundowners happen at hippo height with the Zimbabwe escarpment going orange opposite.
places.neighborhood: Chiawa Camp, the Zambezi bank west of Jeki

places.name: the Old Mondoro morning walk
places.note: Three hours on foot in a four-tent camp's area with an armed Zambian guide, mostly tracks, dung and birds, with the real chance of walking into buffalo that makes it worth doing.
places.neighborhood: Old Mondoro, the eastern riverbank

places.name: a tiger fishing morning on the Zambezi
places.note: Catch and release for tigerfish from a flat boat, best from about September when the water drops and clears, and it is a lot of casting for not many fish.
places.neighborhood: the main channel off Chiawa and Mwambashi

places.name: dinner on the sandbank at Sausage Tree
places.note: Tables carried out onto an island sandbank with lanterns and a fire, and it is the one meal on this whole route that a restaurant would struggle to beat.
places.neighborhood: Sausage Tree Camp, the Zambezi bank mid-park

places.name: Kanyemba Island
places.note: A grass island that elephant swim to and stand on all afternoon, and drifting the channel behind it is the easiest good hour in the park.
places.neighborhood: a long midstream island opposite the camps

places.name: the Lower Zambezi night drive
places.note: Legal here and not in most Zimbabwean parks, so this is where you get civet, genet, honey badger and the park's regular leopard on the floodplain edge.
places.neighborhood: the Jeki and Chiawa road network after dark

places.name: the Mushika River crossing
places.note: A sand river running out of the escarpment that concentrates elephant and buffalo on the last pools by September, and almost nobody drives this far east.
places.neighborhood: the eastern park boundary, inland from Anabezi

places.name: Long Pool
places.note: Two kilometres of old river channel holding the park's biggest crocodile and hippo concentration, and the ground around it is open enough to walk if your guide likes the wind.
places.neighborhood: Mana Pools, the largest of the four oxbows inland from the r

places.name: Chine Pool
places.note: The quietest of the four pools and the one where the big bulls come to drink in the late afternoon, with an albida fringe that gives you shade to sit in.
places.neighborhood: Mana Pools, the eastern oxbow toward Mana Mouth

places.name: the albida forest walk
places.note: Cathedral-spaced winterthorn on bare ground where the elephant stand on their hind legs to reach the pods, and this is the light every photograph of Mana Pools is taken in.
places.neighborhood: the Faidherbia albida terrace between Nyamepi and the river

places.name: Nyamepi camp and the park office
places.note: Park HQ, the campsite and the desk where you sign the indemnity that lets you walk unguided, which is a right you get here and in almost nowhere else in Africa.
places.neighborhood: Mana Pools headquarters, on the Zambezi bank

places.name: Mana Mouth
places.note: Where the floodplain runs out into the main river, good for a canoe put-in and the one spot with a clear line of sight across to the Zambian bank.
places.neighborhood: the eastern end of the Mana floodplain where the channel rej

places.name: Chitake Springs
places.note: A spring in a dry riverbed that is the only water for a long way, so lion, buffalo and elephant use the same hundred metres of sand, and you watch it on foot from the bank; it needs September or October to be worth the drive.
places.neighborhood: the south of the park under the escarpment, 60 km from the r

places.name: Kanga Pan
places.note: A single pan in dry mopane 30 km back from the Zambezi, which means everything walks to it through the middle of the day while the riverfront is empty.
places.neighborhood: inland Mana, the only permanent water away from the river

places.name: the Mucheni riverfront campsites
places.note: Four unfenced sites straight on the bank with no barrier between your fire and the river, which is the point and also why you do not leave the chairs out.
places.neighborhood: Mana Pools, the exclusive-use sites west of Nyamepi

places.name: the Vundu Camp walking morning
places.note: The camp that trained most of Zimbabwe's professional guides, and a morning here is four hours on foot with someone who will put you on the ground at 30 metres from a bull and explain exactly why it is safe.
places.neighborhood: Vundu Camp, the western riverfront

places.name: the Rukomechi River mouth
places.note: Where a seasonal river runs into the Zambezi at the park's western edge, with hot springs inland and the emptiest stretch of riverfront in Mana.
places.neighborhood: the western boundary of the park

places.name: the Sapi confluence at Chikwenya
places.note: The far east corner where the Sapi comes in, with island channels that hold wild dog most seasons and almost no other vehicles.
places.neighborhood: the eastern park boundary at the Sapi Safari Area

places.name: the canoe leg down the Zambezi
places.note: Canadian canoes on the main river with hippo pods to read and a guide who navigates around them, not through them, and it is genuinely tiring in a headwind.
places.neighborhood: the main channel between Nyamepi and Mana Mouth

places.name: Ngweshla Pan
places.note: A pumped pan on open grass that pulls big elephant herds through the late dry season, and the picnic site beside it is the one place in the park you can legally get out of the vehicle.
places.neighborhood: south-east Hwange, the Ngweshla picnic site and pan

places.name: Kennedy 1 Pan
places.note: One of a chain of pumped pans along a shallow grass vlei, and the lion on this line are the reason the eastern concessions charge what they do.
places.neighborhood: the Kennedy vlei line, south-east Hwange

places.name: the Nyamandhlovu platform
places.note: A raised concrete platform over a pumped pan where you can sit from mid-afternoon and count elephant arriving in waves, and in September and October the numbers are absurd.
places.neighborhood: 10 km west of Main Camp

places.name: the Guvalala platform
places.note: Quieter than Nyamandhlovu and closer to the road junction, worth an hour on the way back to the gate rather than a trip of its own.
places.neighborhood: the Main Camp loop, south-west of Nyamandhlovu

places.name: the elephant pool at Somalisa
places.note: A shallow plunge pool at the edge of camp that elephant drink from over the guests' shoulders, which sounds like a gimmick and is not, because the bulls were coming before the camp was there.
places.neighborhood: Somalisa Camp, the Kennedy vlei acacia plain

places.name: the Makalolo Plains
places.note: Open Kalahari grassland with a line of pans across it, and it is the part of the park with the best chance of wild dog on a morning drive.
places.neighborhood: the central-southern concession, around Little Makalolo and

places.name: Hwange Main Camp
places.note: The park's old rest camp and entry gate, run down and short of money, and unless you are self-driving there is no reason to stop here beyond paying the fee.
places.neighborhood: the eastern park gate off the Bulawayo road

places.name: Dete Vlei
places.note: A long open vlei outside the park boundary where the elephant cross the railway at dusk, and the light on the grass at six in the morning is the best in the region.
places.neighborhood: the grassland corridor along the railway line north-east of

places.name: the Painted Dog Conservation centre
places.note: A rehabilitation and anti-snaring project with a small interpretive centre, and the wall of wire snares removed from this park does more than any lecture could.
places.neighborhood: the Dete road just outside the Main Camp gate

places.name: the Masuma Dam hide
places.note: A hide and campsite above a dam in the rocky north of the park, five hours from the southern concessions and worth it only if you are driving yourself.
places.neighborhood: northern Hwange, on the Sinamatella road

places.name: the Ngamo Plains
places.note: Treeless Kalahari plain that looks like Serengeti for about eight weeks after the rains and like a dust bowl for the rest of the year, so it depends entirely on when you come.
places.neighborhood: the south-eastern corner of the park

places.name: the sunken hide at The Hide
places.note: A tunnel from camp into a log-and-earth hide at water level on the pan, so you sit under the elephants' feet through the heat of the day with a cold drink.
places.neighborhood: The Hide Safari Camp, the Kennedy area

outings.fallback: The bridge walk and the Lookout Cafe gorge terrace, which give you the second gorge without the spray.

outings.name: the Batoka Gorge, Rapid 1 to 25

outings.fallback: A short walk from the vehicle on the river sand, which most Mfuwe camps will do on request.

outings.why: Leave at four, watch the sun go down on the river, then two hours under a filtered spotlight. Zambia allows this and Zimbabwe's national parks largely do not, which is why leopard here is a near certainty rather than a hope.
outings.name: the Luangwa night drive out of Mfuwe Gate
outings.season: All year where camps are open. Best June to October; roads i
outings.fallback: The afternoon drive only, back through the gate by dusk, which still gets you the river crossings.

outings.why: A short drive and a crawl into a two-tier hide cut into the riverbank a few metres from around sixty hippo. You are below eye level with them for two hours and you cannot leave until they move off. Shenton guests only, so it decides where y
outings.name: the Kaingo hippo hide at dawn
outings.season: June to early November while Kaingo is open.
outings.fallback: The elephant hide at the river crossing, or the mobile hide at the waterhole.

outings.why: Three to four hours in a Canadian canoe down a side channel behind the islands, reading hippo pods and going around them. Water level at your elbow and elephant on both banks. It is low risk with a good guide and high risk with a cheap one,
outings.name: canoeing the Chifungulu Channel
outings.season: Roughly May to mid-November while the camps are open. The ch
outings.fallback: A motorboat drift on the main channel, which loses the silence but keeps the birds.

outings.why: Out on foot from the river terrace through open winterthorn to the biggest of the four oxbows, four hours with a professional guide or on your own if you sign the indemnity at Nyamepi. Zimbabwe's guide qualification is the hardest in Africa
outings.name: the Long Pool walk in the albida
outings.season: Roughly April to November. The park is effectively shut Janu
outings.fallback: A short walk from the vehicle along the Mucheni riverfront, or a sit at Chine Pool through the afternoon.

outings.why: Two hours of rough track south to a spring in a dry riverbed that is the only water for a long way, then hours sitting above the sand watching lion, buffalo and elephant use the same hundred metres. It is the most dangerous ground in this c
outings.name: Chitake Springs
outings.season: September and October, when everything else has dried out. P
outings.fallback: Kanga Pan, which is a softer version of the same idea and a lot closer to the river.

outings.why: A morning on the main Zambezi in a Canadian canoe with lunch on a sandbank. The hippo are the work and the headwind after eleven is the other work, so it goes early and stops early.
outings.name: the canoe leg from Nyamepi to Mana Mouth
outings.season: April to November. Best June to September before the heat.
outings.fallback: A two hour paddle in the backwater behind the islands, which keeps the wind off.

outings.why: A full day working the pumped pans along the southern vlei line with a packed lunch at Ngweshla, where you can get out of the vehicle. In September and October the elephant come in herds of several hundred and the water is the only reason a
outings.name: the Ngweshla and Kennedy pan circuit
outings.season: July to early November. From December the pans fill with rai
outings.fallback: An afternoon at the camp waterhole or the sunken hide, which needs no driving at all.

outings.why: Drive out mid-afternoon, climb the platform and stay until the gate time forces you back. It is concrete, there are other people on it, and it is still the highest elephant count you will get standing still anywhere on this trip.
outings.name: the Nyamandhlovu platform afternoon
outings.season: August to November for the numbers. Half empty in the rains.
outings.fallback: The Guvalala platform, nearer the junction and usually deserted.

outings.why: Six kilometres upstream of the falls, a riverside track with sable, elephant and very few vehicles, which is the only actual game viewing you can do from a bed in Victoria Falls town. Two hours of driving for a decent chance at not much.
outings.name: the Zambezi National Park river drive
outings.season: All year. Best in the dry, June to October.
outings.fallback: The Mosi-oa-Tunya rhino block on the Zambian side, which at least guarantees you rhino.

outings.why: A 111 metre bungee off the middle of the 1905 arch, a gorge swing off the Zimbabwe abutment, or a guided walk under the deck on the maintenance catwalk if you would rather keep your breakfast. You can do the bridge walk itself for nothing b
outings.name: the bridge: bungee, swing and the catwalk
outings.season: All year. The catwalk tour runs roughly 08:00 to 17:00.
outings.fallback: The free walk to the middle of the bridge and back, which is the best free thing at the falls.

destination.name: Zambia and Zimbabwe: the Zambezi
destination.pitch: One waterfall seen from two countries, then four river parks where the walking is the point, and the whole thing rises or falls on which month you pick.
destination.caveat: Every leg between the parks is a light aircraft booked months ahead at USD 400 to 700 a seat, the good camps run USD 450 to 900 per person per night and sell out a year out for September and October, and the falls swing so hard between the April flood and the November low that the same ticket buys t Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Livingstone and Victoria Falls town are supply towns with a waterfall attached, and neither repays more than an evening of your time.
because.food: Camp cooking is set menu and competent and the only real restaurants are in two small towns, so eat properly at the falls and lower your expectations after that.
because.nature: The Luangwa holds the densest leopard population in Africa, the Lower Zambezi and Mana Pools face each other across one river with elephant swimming between them, and Hwange's pumped pans concentrate several hundred elephant on a single pan
because.culture: The Livingstone Museum is franker about the colonial record than most in the region, the Leya chieftaincy at Mukuni predates the town by centuries, and the Luangwa camps are largely Zambian owned and Zambian guided.
because.adventure: Devil's Pool on the lip of a 108 metre drop when the water drops, grade five water through the Batoka Gorge, and unaccompanied walking that is legal in Mana Pools and almost nowhere else in Africa.
because.relaxation: Three nights on a Lower Zambezi deck with a canoe instead of a vehicle, no phone signal and hippo at eye level, is the closest this catalogue gets to a full stop.
because.exploration: Four rivers, two sides of one gorge and an international border you cross on foot in the middle of the trip, with the Zambian and Zimbabwean halves run on completely different rules.
